title: The Search Engine for the Agentic Web — Will Bryk, Exa
talk_summary: Will Bryk pitches Exa as a search engine purpose-built for AI agents, arguing agents need database-like retrieval (embeddings + keywords, structured output, token extraction) rather than human-oriented keyword search. The talk is mostly vision and mission; the only concrete mechanisms are retrieval-API design choices and token-efficient extraction.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of returning full documents, Exa returns only the most important ~100 tokens per document so the downstream LLM consumes less context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we'll give you only the most important like 100 tokens from those documents. And that will save you a lot of downstream LLM costs

takeaways.what_they_do: Search returns typed fields (e.g., paper, college, graduation year) directly rather than snippets the model must parse.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We'll just give you that as structured output. It makes it really easy.

takeaways.what_they_do: Exa exposes both a 200ms fast endpoint and slower high-quality modes, letting each customer pick the tradeoff.
Combine keyword search (efficient, simple queries) with embeddings (semantic, complex queries) rather than relying on either alone.
takeaways.evidence_quote: often you want to combine embeddings and keywords
